mainEntity.name: What should I consider when planning an in-law suite or multigenerational space?

acceptedAnswer.text: Building an in-law suite requires balancing privacy, accessibility, and utility infrastructure. A practical trade-off exists between attached additions and detached accessory units: attached suites share plumbing and central climate systems more easily, while detached buildings maximize physical privacy but demand separate utility hookups. Consider incorporating universal design features such as curbless walk-in showers and wider doorways early during planning. In addition, evaluate whether the occupant requires an independent kitchenette or simply an enlarged bedroom with a dedicated bathroom, as cooking facilities introduce distinct plumbing and permitting factors.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider occupant privacy, accessibility needs like walk-in showers, separate utility connections, and whether you require an independent kitchenette or an attached guest bedroom suite.
